From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing

Joe — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we have a shared record. Main points I captured: 

- Expected token profile: ~50M tokens/month for first 3 months, scaling to ~300–500M tokens/month in 6–12 months. Peak bursts observed in product telemetry: spikes up to ~20–30M tokens over a 1–2 hour window during promotions.
- Primary requirement: low-latency generation for chat (95th pct < 500ms) and the ability to absorb bursts without failed requests.
- Budget guidance you gave: target ~$10k–$30k/mo initially, with flexibility if unit economics scale favorably. You asked for a target $/1M-tokens to evaluate.

Action items I promised:
1) Email over a proposed pricing/overage structure (committed tiers + overage) and the burst/quota increase process.
2) Share a mutual action plan (timeline, approvals, POC criteria).
3) Loop in procurement if we need contract language.

I've attached a short pricing sheet (ACME_Redwood_Pricing_v1.pdf) and a draft MAD (attached). High-level pricing proposal below — this is aligned to the volumes you described and optimized to hit target unit economics near ~$30/1M tokens after commit: 

- No-commit (pay-as-you-go): $55 per 1M tokens; overage charged at $65 per 1M beyond soft quota.
- Committed 6-month tier (recommended for expected scale): $28 per 1M tokens for committed volume (min 300M over 6 months), overage at $40 per 1M.
- Reserved / Dedicated discussions available for 1M+ tokens/day steady workloads — we can run a dedicated pricing model if you want predictable latency and cheaper unit cost.

Rate limits / quota & burst handling: 
- Default API quotas: token-per-minute quota and request-per-second (RPS) caps per API key. Example default: 5k RPS / 10M tokens per minute for high-tier accounts (we can tailor).
- Burst policy: customers on committed tiers can request temporary burst increases (up to 3x typical quota) with 24–72 hour notice for auto-approval; for unplanned bursts we provide a limited short-duration buffer (soft-burst) to absorb spikes and avoid 429s.
- Overage handling: soft-quota throttles and alerting at 80/95% of quota; overage billed monthly at agreed overage rate.

If that looks reasonable, next step: confirm which pricing path you want us to model (pay-as-you-go vs 6mo commit) and we'll produce a formal quote and MAD timeline.

Thanks — talking points for the demo on Thursday are in the attached MAD.

— Rafael

Joe — thanks, great questions. I ran a quick blended model and included it in the attached pricing PDF, but summary numbers below: 

Blended $/1M tokens (examples):
- PAYG: flat $55/1M — blended is the same regardless of volume.
- Committed 6mo (example commit = 300M over 6 months = 50M/mo): committed price $28/1M for committed volume; overage $40/1M. If you hit 300M/mo (steady) the blended goes to ~$28/1M; at 300M in a month + 50M overage, blended ~ $31/1M.
- Commit + scale example (if you commit to 1.8B over 6 months = avg 300M/mo but scale within months): effective blended can get to mid-$20s per 1M once commit thresholds and sustained usage are met.

Example blended math (simple):
- At 300M tokens/month on the 6mo committed model (all within commit) — effective = $28/1M.
- At 500M tokens/month with commit = 300M and 200M overage: (300M * $28 + 200M * $40) / 500M = $32.8/1M.

Burst policy (operational detail):
- Auto-burst: for committed accounts we provide a soft auto-burst buffer (typically 1.5–2x) to absorb short spikes without 429s.
- Temporary quota increases: submit a request 24–72 hours before expected spike via the Console or the SLA escalation channel; we'll auto-approve up to 3x quota for the window.
- Emergency short-notice bursts: we will attempt to grant a short emergency buffer (limits apply); this can incur a one-time surge fee if it exceeds agreed soft-burst allowances. Fee = higher overage rate for that burst window (typically +25% on the standard overage rate). We can bake specific language into the contract.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rafael/Marissa to produce a short two-sheet: (a) formal quote with line items and blended examples at 300M/500M and (b) suggested contract language for burst / emergency surges.
2) Acme to confirm which commit level you'd like modeled (300M over 6 months vs a lighter 150M/6mo).
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement call next week to walk redlines.

I'll have the two-sheet ready by end-of-day tomorrow. If agreeable, Camila can start the MAD timeline and loop in legal.

— Rafael

Joe / team — quick ops note from the engineering side on how we handle quotas and burst safety: 

- Instrumentation & alerts: Console will emit quota warnings at 80% and 95% and can push Slack/webhook alerts to your SRE channel.
- Smooth degradation: when a quota is reached we prefer returning 429 with Retry-After for headroom; for committed customers we route overflow to compatible model variants where possible to avoid hard failures.
- Burst testing: we recommend a short stress test during POC (we can schedule a controlled 2-hour ramp to validate both latency and burst handling).
- Quota increases: internal SLA for approving scheduled increases is 24–72 hours; emergency increases require a quick support escalation and may include a surge fee if beyond soft-burst allowances.

Happy to run the stress test and post results in the MAD as accept criteria.

— Marissa
